shipments.detail: The Shipments search vocabulary: the 27 attributes the search BAR understands across 10 groups, plus what the FILTERS PANEL offers — which, for Shipments, is the same 27 attributes, because the panel is generated directly from the progression. Everything on the Attributes sheet marked Implemented is live on Vercel; everything on Not Implemented is a stakeholder proposal that was not built.

This workbook is GENERATED from apps/odyssey-one/src/search/shipments/progression.js — it cannot drift from what is deployed. Pickup # is no longer marked skipped: it shipped in S104 and is now Implemented (see the Attributes sheet).

The Attributes and Progression sheets carry both a "Group (filters panel header)" and a "Suggestions panel header" column. Shipments renders group.group as the filters panel's section header and group.label as the suggestions panel's section title — different strings for the same group, both real, both in the UI.

Shipments has TWO label sets for a group, not three: the suggestions panel section title (group.label, e.g. "Find the shipment") and the bar/filters-panel section header (group.group, e.g. "Shipment Identifiers") — because the filters panel is generated directly from the progression, that second label doubles as the panel's own section header too. Contrast Orders, which has three (see that workbook's Open Questions).

shipments.topic: Where the attribute list came from
shipments.detail: A 2026-05 stakeholder grouping session proposed a taxonomy; the app implements 27 of those attributes plus 3 the stakeholder sheet never proposed (Order Count, Shipment Type, Planning Type). 22 proposed attributes were not built — see Not Implemented.

The bar's suggestion list is ORDERED, not restricted. Empty bar → suggests group 1. Commit a chip from group N → the empty-bar suggestion advances to the next group. It never blocks a chip combination, and typing always value-matches across all 27 attributes regardless of group.

The bar's bare-text search only reaches the attributes in FREE_TEXT_KEYS (search/shipments/criteria.js) — identifiers and party/place names a user would paste or type by name. Measures and enums are reachable as chips, not as free text.

Progression = the 10 groups. Attributes = the 27 implemented + 22 not-built attributes. Match Types = the shared matching vocabulary. Panel Filters = the panel's field list. Not Implemented = the stakeholder proposals that never shipped. Open Questions = what needs a Jana/Shipments or design-system decision.

orders.detail: The Orders search vocabulary: the 20 attributes the search BAR understands across 9 groups, and the 13 filters the PANEL offers. Everything here is implemented and test-pinned in the React prototype.

Unlike Shipments, Orders has TWO separate catalogs: the bar (progression.js, 20 attributes, flat) and the panel (registry.js, 13 fields, flat since ORD-23). A new Orders attribute does not automatically become a panel field the way it does for Shipments — see Open Questions.

Orders has THREE label sets for the same field: the suggestions panel section title (progression group.label, e.g. "Find the order"), the bar's own grouping (progression group.group, e.g. "Customers & Parties"), and the filters panel's section header (registry group, e.g. "Order Identifiers" — where Customer and Order Status actually sit). The Panel Filters and Attributes sheets carry a "Panel section" column so the three never get conflated. See Open Questions.
This workbook is GENERATED from apps/odyssey-one/src/search/orders/progression.js and registry.js — it cannot drift from what is deployed.

orders.topic: Where the bar list came from
orders.detail: Every column on all three Orders tabs, and nothing else (S130 ruling: 'Orders have its own columns, that is why we are defining its own progression'). A column with no attribute = a field you cannot search by; an attribute with no column = a field nobody can see to type.

The bar's suggestion list is ORDERED, not restricted. Empty bar → suggests group 1. Commit a chip from group N → the empty-bar suggestion advances to the next group. It never blocks a chip combination, and typing always matches values across all 20 attributes regardless of group.

Ship Direction is stored 'O'/'I' but the chip says Outbound/Inbound — same pattern for Freight Terms, Order Source and Hazardous. The row is projected to display labels and the matcher compares labels, so a chip reads the way the column reads.

Progression = the 9 groups. Attributes = the 20 implemented + 4 not-built row fields. Match Types = the shared matching vocabulary. Panel Filters = the 13 panel fields. Not Implemented = row fields deliberately excluded from search. Open Questions = what needs a Ramesh/Orders decision.
